In arXiv 2410.04772, the model skeleton differs from the training procedure in that access to the model skeleton allows an auditor to understand the specific model class used (e.g., neural network architecture) and the interactions between different components of the AI system, including expected inputs and outputs. This provides a clear view of the model's structure and how it processes information.

In contrast, access to the training procedure provides details about how the AI system was developed, including the model class, objective function, hyperparameter tuning, and quality checks. However, while the training procedure offers insights into the development process, it does not directly reveal the final behavior of the model, as the resulting model can vary significantly based on other factors like training data and initialization.

Thus, the model skeleton offers a more interpretable view of the AI system's architecture and functionality, while the training procedure provides a roadmap of the development process but does not guarantee insights into the model's ultimate behavior.
